items.stem: Define the term “a primary alcohol”.
items.answer: An alcohol in which the –OH group is attached to a carbon bonded to one other carbon.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: an alcohol in which the –OH group is attached to a carbon bonded to one other carbon.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about nomenclature and preparation of alcohols and phenols is correct?
items.answer: Phenol is made commercially from cumene.
items.markingKey: (b) Phenol is made commercially from cumene. The other statements are false. It follows Markovnikov's rule and gives propan-2-ol. Reduction of a ketone gives a secondary alcohol, propan-2-ol. Ethanal gives a secondary alcohol, propan-2-ol.
options: Phenol is made commercially from cumene.
Hydration of propene in acid gives propan-1-ol.
Ethanal gives a tertiary alcohol with CH₃MgBr.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a primary alcohol?
items.answer: 4-nitrophenol
items.markingKey: (c) 4-nitrophenol is a phenol, not a primary alcohol.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “Ethanal gives a tertiary alcohol with CH₃MgBr.”
items.answer: Ethanal gives a secondary alcohol, propan-2-ol.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: Ethanal gives a secondary alcohol, propan-2-ol.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about nomenclature and preparation of alcohols and phenols is incorrect?
items.answer: Ethanal gives a tertiary alcohol with CH₃MgBr.
items.markingKey: (a) The incorrect statement is “Ethanal gives a tertiary alcohol with CH₃MgBr.” Correct form: Ethanal gives a secondary alcohol, propan-2-ol.
options: Ethanal gives a tertiary alcohol with CH₃MgBr.
In alcohols the C–O–H bond angle is slightly less than tetrahedral.
Phenol is made commercially from cumene.
Ketones give tertiary alcohols with Grignard reagents.

items.stem:
Anil prepares phenol by the cumene process in a project report.
(i) Write the starting material and the intermediate. (1 mark)
(ii) What is the by-product and why is it useful? (1 mark)
(iii) Give two other laboratory methods to make phenol. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) Cumene (isopropylbenzene); cumene hydroperoxide. (ii) Propanone (acetone), a valuable solvent. (iii) From chlorobenzene (NaOH, 623 K, 300 atm) or from benzenesulphonic acid (NaOH fusion) or from benzenediazonium chloride (warm water).

items.stem: Which of the following is a secondary alcohol?
items.answer: butan-2-ol
items.markingKey: (c) Butan-2-ol is a secondary alcohol; the others are not.

items.stem: Which structure corresponds to prop-2-en-1-ol?
items.answer: CH₂=CHCH₂OH
items.markingKey: (d) prop-2-en-1-ol = CH₂=CHCH₂OH.

items.stem: Classify each of the following as secondary alcohol or phenol: cyclohexanol, 2-methylphenol, benzene-1,3-diol, butan-2-ol.
items.answer: cyclohexanol – secondary alcohol; 2-methylphenol – phenol; benzene-1,3-diol – phenol; butan-2-ol – secondary alcohol.
items.markingKey: ½ mark each: cyclohexanol – secondary alcohol; 2-methylphenol – phenol; benzene-1,3-diol – phenol; butan-2-ol – secondary alcohol.

items.stem: What is the IUPAC name of (CH₃)₃COH?
items.answer: 2-methylpropan-2-ol
items.markingKey: (CH₃)₃COH = 2-methylpropan-2-ol.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Methanal gives a primary alcohol with a Grignard reagent.
Reason (R): Hydration of propene in acid gives propan-1-ol.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is true, but R is false.
items.markingKey: (c) A is true. R is false: It follows Markovnikov's rule and gives propan-2-ol.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Show how propan-2-ol and 2-methylpropan-2-ol can be prepared using Grignard reagents.
items.answer: Propan-2-ol: CH₃CHO + CH₃MgBr → (CH₃)₂CHOMgBr → (H₂O) (CH₃)₂CHOH. 2-Methylpropan-2-ol: CH₃COCH₃ + CH₃MgBr → (CH₃)₃COMgBr → (H₂O) (CH₃)₃COH.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a tertiary alcohol?
items.answer: propan-2-ol
items.markingKey: (a) Propan-2-ol is a secondary alcohol, not a tertiary alcohol.

items.stem: Write the product formed when chlorobenzene is treated with NaOH at 623 K and 300 atm, then dilute HCl, and name the process or principle.
items.answer: Phenol; Dow process
items.markingKey: Phenol (1); Dow process (1).

items.stem: Which term describes an alcohol in which the –OH group is attached to a carbon bonded to one other carbon?
items.answer: a primary alcohol
items.markingKey: (c) A primary alcohol: an alcohol in which the –OH group is attached to a carbon bonded to one other carbon.

items.stem: What is meant by “esterification”?
items.answer: The reaction of an alcohol or phenol with a carboxylic acid, acid chloride or anhydride to form an ester.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the reaction of an alcohol or phenol with a carboxylic acid, acid chloride or anhydride to form an ester.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about properties of alcohols and phenols; acidity is correct?
items.answer: Boiling points of alcohols decrease with branching.
items.markingKey: (d) Boiling points of alcohols decrease with branching. The other statements are false. Phenol is more acidic; the phenoxide ion is resonance-stabilised. o-Nitrophenol is steam volatile; p-nitrophenol forms intermolecular hydrogen bonds. They decrease acidity; cresols are weaker acids than phenol.
options: Electron-donating groups such as –CH₃ increase the acidity of phenol.
p-Nitrophenol is steam volatile because of intramolecular hydrogen bonding.
Ethanol is more acidic than phenol.
Boiling points of alcohols decrease with branching.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Phenol is more acidic than ethanol.
Reason (R): Primary alcohols give immediate turbidity with Lucas reagent.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is true, but R is false.
items.markingKey: (c) A is true. R is false: Tertiary alcohols give immediate turbidity; primary alcohols react only on heating.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “Electron-donating groups such as –CH₃ increase the acidity of phenol.”
items.answer: They decrease acidity; cresols are weaker acids than phenol.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: They decrease acidity; cresols are weaker acids than phenol.

items.stem: Given the pKa values ethanol 15.9, 2,4,6-trinitrophenol 0.5, m-nitrophenol 8.3, o-nitrophenol 7.2, which compound is the most acidic?
items.answer: 2,4,6-trinitrophenol
items.markingKey: (c) Lower pKa means stronger acid: 2,4,6-trinitrophenol (pKa 0.5) is the most acidic.

items.stem: What is the main product when 2-methylpropan-2-ol reacts with Cu at 573 K?
items.answer: 2-methylpropene
items.markingKey: (c) 2-methylpropene: a 3° alcohol undergoes dehydration.
options: a mixture of o- and p-nitrophenol
a mixture of o- and p-bromophenol

items.stem:
Tanvi is given three unlabelled alcohols of formula C₄H₁₀O: butan-1-ol, butan-2-ol and 2-methylpropan-2-ol. She adds Lucas reagent to each.
(i) What is Lucas reagent? (1 mark)
(ii) Predict the observation for each. (2 marks)
(iii) Explain the order of reactivity. (1 mark)
items.answer: (i) Conc. HCl with anhydrous ZnCl₂. (ii) 2-Methylpropan-2-ol: turbidity at once; butan-2-ol: turbidity in about 5 minutes; butan-1-ol: no turbidity at room temperature. (iii) Reaction goes via carbocations; stability 3° > 2° > 1°.

items.stem: Explain why the presence of a nitro group at the ortho or para position increases the acidity of phenol.
items.answer: The –NO₂ group withdraws electrons by –R and –I effects; at o/p positions the negative charge of the phenoxide ion is delocalised onto the nitro group, which stabilises the ion and makes the release of H⁺ easier.
items.markingKey: 1 mark effect; 1 mark stabilisation of phenoxide.

items.stem: Arrange the following in the correct order of boiling point: propanal, methoxyethane, butane, propan-1-ol. Give a reason.
items.answer: butane < methoxyethane < propanal < propan-1-ol
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the order butane < methoxyethane < propanal < propan-1-ol; 1 mark for the reason: Intermolecular hydrogen bonding in alcohols gives the highest boiling point.

items.stem: Write the main product when ethanol reacts with ethanoic acid with a few drops of conc. H₂SO₄, and name the reaction or give the reason.
items.answer: Ethyl ethanoate; esterification
items.markingKey: Ethyl ethanoate (1); esterification (1).

items.stem: Which term describes the reaction of sodium phenoxide with CO₂ under pressure to give salicylic acid?
items.answer: the Kolbe reaction
items.markingKey: (b) The Kolbe reaction: the reaction of sodium phenoxide with CO₂ under pressure to give salicylic acid.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): o-Nitrophenol has a lower boiling point than p-nitrophenol.
Reason (R): o-Nitrophenol has intramolecular hydrogen bonding.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) p-Isomer has intermolecular H-bonding and higher b.p.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: The pKa of o-nitrophenol is 7.2. Calculate its Ka and the pH of a 0.1 M aqueous solution (assume weak acid, α ≪ 1).
Write the main product when 2-methylpropan-2-ol reacts with Cu at 573 K, and name the reaction or give the reason.
items.answer: 2-methylpropene; a 3° alcohol undergoes dehydration
items.markingKey: 2-methylpropene (1); a 3° alcohol undergoes dehydration (1).

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “p-Nitrophenol is steam volatile because of intramolecular hydrogen bonding.”
items.answer: o-Nitrophenol is steam volatile; p-nitrophenol forms intermolecular hydrogen bonds.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: o-Nitrophenol is steam volatile; p-nitrophenol forms intermolecular hydrogen bonds.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Tertiary alcohols react fastest with the Lucas reagent.
Reason (R): Primary alcohols give immediate turbidity with Lucas reagent.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is true, but R is false.
items.markingKey: (c) A is true. R is false: Tertiary alcohols give immediate turbidity; primary alcohols react only on heating.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: What is meant by “Lucas test”?
items.answer: A test with conc. HCl and anhydrous ZnCl₂ in which 3° alcohols give immediate turbidity, 2° in about five minutes and 1° only on heating.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: a test with conc. HCl and anhydrous ZnCl₂ in which 3° alcohols give immediate turbidity, 2° in about five minutes and 1° only on heating.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about properties of alcohols and phenols; acidity is correct?
items.answer: Tertiary alcohols react fastest with the Lucas reagent.
items.markingKey: (d) Tertiary alcohols react fastest with the Lucas reagent. The other statements are false. Phenol is more acidic; the phenoxide ion is resonance-stabilised. o-Nitrophenol is steam volatile; p-nitrophenol forms intermolecular hydrogen bonds. They decrease acidity; cresols are weaker acids than phenol.
options: Ethanol is more acidic than phenol.
p-Nitrophenol is steam volatile because of intramolecular hydrogen bonding.
Electron-donating groups such as –CH₃ increase the acidity of phenol.
Tertiary alcohols react fastest with the Lucas reagent.

items.stem: What is meant by “fermentation”?
items.answer: The slow breakdown of sugars into ethanol and CO₂ by enzymes from yeast.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the slow breakdown of sugars into ethanol and CO₂ by enzymes from yeast.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about commercially important alcohols is correct?
items.answer: Air is kept out during fermentation.
items.markingKey: (a) Air is kept out during fermentation. The other statements are false. Methanol is highly poisonous and can cause blindness and death. Invertase first hydrolyses sucrose; zymase then converts glucose and fructose into ethanol. Copper sulphate (colour) and pyridine (smell) are added.
options: Air is kept out during fermentation.
Denatured alcohol is made by adding sugar to ethanol.
Zymase converts sucrose directly into ethanol.
Methanol is safe to drink in small amounts.

items.stem: Write the equations for the preparation of methanol from synthesis gas and of ethanol from sucrose.
items.answer: CO + 2H₂ → CH₃OH (ZnO–Cr₂O₃, 200–300 atm, 573–673 K). C₁₂H₂₂O₁₁ + H₂O → C₆H₁₂O₆ + C₆H₁₂O₆ (invertase); C₆H₁₂O₆ → 2C₂H₅OH + 2CO₂ (zymase).
items.markingKey: 1 mark each.

items.stem: At a sugar mill near Kolhapur, Tara ferments 18.0 kg of glucose with yeast (zymase): C₆H₁₂O₆ → 2C₂H₅OH + 2CO₂. If the yield is 90%, calculate the mass of ethanol formed and the volume of CO₂ at STP (22.7 L mol⁻¹).
items.answer: 8.28 kg ethanol; 4090 L CO₂

items.stem:
An important alcohol has these features: by-product of soap manufacture; very viscous with a high boiling point; used in cosmetics and to make nitroglycerine.
(i) Identify the alcohol. (1 mark)
(ii) State one more feature you would expect to observe. (1 mark)
(iii) How would the observations differ if it were methanol? Give two points. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) Glycerol (propane-1,2,3-triol) (ii) has three –OH groups (iii) used as a solvent and to make methanal; called wood spirit
items.markingKey: (i) glycerol (propane-1,2,3-triol) – 1 mark. (ii) any one of: has three –OH groups – 1 mark. (iii) for methanol: called wood spirit; made from CO and H₂ at 573–673 K over ZnO–Cr₂O₃; used as a solvent and to make methanal – 1 mark each for any two.

items.stem: Arrange the following in the correct sequence in the manufacture of ethanol from molasses: ethanol + CO₂ (zymase), glucose + fructose (invertase), sucrose (molasses). Give a reason.
items.answer: sucrose (molasses) → glucose + fructose (invertase) → ethanol + CO₂ (zymase)
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the order sucrose (molasses) → glucose + fructose (invertase) → ethanol + CO₂ (zymase); 1 mark for the reason: Invertase hydrolyses sucrose; zymase ferments the hexoses.

items.stem: An important alcohol has these features: used as a solvent and to make methanal; called wood spirit. Identify the alcohol. Give a reason.
items.answer: Methanol
items.markingKey: 1 mark: methanol; 1 mark: the features used as a solvent and to make methanal; called wood spirit are characteristic of it.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about commercially important alcohols is incorrect?
items.answer: Zymase converts sucrose directly into ethanol.
items.markingKey: (b) The incorrect statement is “Zymase converts sucrose directly into ethanol.” Correct form: Invertase first hydrolyses sucrose; zymase then converts glucose and fructose into ethanol.
options: Air is kept out during fermentation.
Zymase converts sucrose directly into ethanol.
Methanol is made industrially from CO and H₂ over a ZnO–Cr₂O₃ catalyst.
Drinking even small amounts of methanol can cause blindness.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “Denatured alcohol is made by adding sugar to ethanol.”
items.answer: Copper sulphate (colour) and pyridine (smell) are added.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: Copper sulphate (colour) and pyridine (smell) are added.

items.stem: What is denatured alcohol?
items.answer: Ethanol made unfit for drinking by adding copper sulphate and pyridine.
items.markingKey: 1 mark.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Denatured alcohol is made by adding sugar to ethanol.
Reason (R): Methanol is made industrially from CO and H₂ over a ZnO–Cr₂O₃ catalyst.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A is false: Copper sulphate (colour) and pyridine (smell) are added. R is a true statement.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Commercial alcohol is coloured blue and has a foul smell.
Reason (R): Copper sulphate and pyridine are added to it.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) Denatured alcohol cannot be drunk.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Define the term “anisole”.
items.answer: Methoxybenzene, C₆H₅OCH₃.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: methoxybenzene, C₆H₅OCH₃.

items.stem: What is the IUPAC name of C₂H₅OC₂H₅?
items.answer: ethoxyethane
items.markingKey: (c) C₂H₅OC₂H₅ = ethoxyethane.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Ethers have lower boiling points than isomeric alcohols.
Reason (R): Anisole gives iodobenzene and methanol with HI.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is true, but R is false.
items.markingKey: (c) A is true. R is false: It gives phenol and iodomethane; the aryl–O bond is not broken.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “Ethers are more soluble in water than alcohols of similar mass.”
items.answer: They are similar in solubility to alcohols for small members but cannot donate H-bonds; boiling points are much lower.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: They are similar in solubility to alcohols for small members but cannot donate H-bonds; boiling points are much lower.

items.stem: What are the main products when ethoxyethane reacts with excess hot conc. HI?
items.answer: iodoethane (2 mol)
items.markingKey: (b) Iodoethane (2 mol): both C–O bonds are cleaved.

items.stem:
Rakesh heats methoxyethane and, separately, anisole with hydrogen iodide.
(i) Write the products in each case. (2 marks)
(ii) Why does anisole not give iodobenzene? (1 mark)
(iii) Which product forms from tert-butyl methyl ether, and by which mechanism? (1 mark)
items.answer: (i) Methoxyethane: CH₃I + C₂H₅OH; anisole: C₆H₅OH + CH₃I. (ii) The C(aryl)–O bond has partial double bond character and the sp² carbon resists SN attack. (iii) (CH₃)₃CI + CH₃OH by SN1.

items.stem: Which structure corresponds to 2-methoxypropane?
items.answer: (CH₃)₂CHOCH₃
items.markingKey: (a) 2-methoxypropane = (CH₃)₂CHOCH₃.

items.stem: Of the two ways of making 2-methoxy-2-methylpropane by Williamson synthesis, which is correct? Explain with equations.
items.answer: (CH₃)₃CONa + CH₃Br → (CH₃)₃COCH₃ + NaBr. The alternative (CH₃)₃CBr + CH₃ONa gives mainly 2-methylpropene because the 3° halide undergoes elimination with the strong base.
items.markingKey: 1 mark correct pair; 1 mark reason with equation.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about ethers is correct?
items.answer: The C–O–C bond angle in ethers is a little more than tetrahedral.
items.markingKey: (b) The C–O–C bond angle in ethers is a little more than tetrahedral. The other statements are false. It gives phenol and iodomethane; the aryl–O bond is not broken. They are similar in solubility to alcohols for small members but cannot donate H-bonds; boiling points are much lower. It is o/p-directing and activating.
options: The C–O–C bond angle in ethers is a little more than tetrahedral.
Ethers are more soluble in water than alcohols of similar mass.
Anisole gives iodobenzene and methanol with HI.

items.stem: Write equations for (i) Williamson synthesis of ethoxyethane, (ii) reaction of methoxyethane with HI, (iii) bromination of anisole, (iv) Friedel–Crafts methylation of anisole, (v) nitration of anisole.
items.answer: (i) C₂H₅ONa + C₂H₅Br → C₂H₅OC₂H₅ + NaBr. (ii) CH₃OC₂H₅ + HI → CH₃I + C₂H₅OH. (iii) Br₂ in CH₃COOH → 4-bromoanisole (major) + 2-bromoanisole. (iv) CH₃Cl/AlCl₃ → 2- and 4-methoxytoluene. (v) Conc. HNO₃/H₂SO₄ → 4-nitroanisole (major) + 2-nitroanisole.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Anisole reacts with HI to give phenol and iodomethane.
Reason (R): The aryl carbon–oxygen bond has partial double bond character.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) So only the methyl–O bond is broken.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Which term describes an ether in which the two groups attached to oxygen are different?
items.answer: an unsymmetrical ether
items.markingKey: (b) An unsymmetrical ether: an ether in which the two groups attached to oxygen are different.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “Anisole gives iodobenzene and methanol with HI.”
items.answer: It gives phenol and iodomethane; the aryl–O bond is not broken.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: It gives phenol and iodomethane; the aryl–O bond is not broken.

items.stem: Which pair of reactants is best for preparing methoxyethane by Williamson synthesis?
items.answer: CH₃CH₂ONa + CH₃Br (or CH₃ONa + CH₃CH₂Br)
items.markingKey: (d) CH₃CH₂ONa + CH₃Br (or CH₃ONa + CH₃CH₂Br): the alkyl halide should be primary (or methyl) for SN2; both halides are primary/methyl, so SN2 works either way.
options: CH₃CH₂OH + CH₃OH with conc. H₂SO₄ at 413 K

items.stem: Which of the following statements about ethers is correct?
items.answer: Williamson synthesis works best with primary alkyl halides.
items.markingKey: (a) Williamson synthesis works best with primary alkyl halides. The other statements are false. With alkoxides tertiary halides undergo elimination to alkenes. It gives phenol and iodomethane; the aryl–O bond is not broken. They are similar in solubility to alcohols for small members but cannot donate H-bonds; boiling points are much lower.
options: Williamson synthesis works best with primary alkyl halides.
Tertiary alkyl halides give good yields of ethers in Williamson synthesis.
Anisole gives iodobenzene and methanol with HI.
Ethers are more soluble in water than alcohols of similar mass.

items.stem: An important alcohol has these features: called wood spirit; highly poisonous, can cause blindness; used as a solvent and to make methanal. Identify the alcohol. Give a reason.
items.answer: Methanol
items.markingKey: 1 mark: methanol; 1 mark: the features called wood spirit; highly poisonous, can cause blindness; used as a solvent and to make methanal are characteristic of it.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about nomenclature and preparation of alcohols and phenols is correct?
items.answer: Phenol is made commercially from cumene.
items.markingKey: (a) Phenol is made commercially from cumene. The other statements are false. Reduction of a ketone gives a secondary alcohol, propan-2-ol. The C–O bond in phenol is shorter, due to partial double bond character and the sp² carbon. Ethanal gives a secondary alcohol, propan-2-ol.
options: Phenol is made commercially from cumene.
Ethanal gives a tertiary alcohol with CH₃MgBr.
In phenol the C–O bond is longer than in methanol.

items.stem:
An important alcohol has these features: denatured with CuSO₄ and pyridine; enzymes invertase and zymase are used; used in beverages, as solvent and as fuel.
(i) Identify the alcohol. (1 mark)
(ii) State one more feature you would expect to observe. (1 mark)
(iii) How would the observations differ if it were methanol? Give two points. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) Ethanol (ii) made by fermentation of molasses (iii) made from CO and H₂ at 573–673 K over ZnO–Cr₂O₃; highly poisonous, can cause blindness
items.markingKey: (i) ethanol – 1 mark. (ii) any one of: made by fermentation of molasses – 1 mark. (iii) for methanol: called wood spirit; made from CO and H₂ at 573–673 K over ZnO–Cr₂O₃; used as a solvent and to make methanal – 1 mark each for any two.

items.stem: Define the term “Williamson synthesis”.
items.answer: The preparation of ethers by the reaction of an alkyl halide with a sodium alkoxide or phenoxide.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the preparation of ethers by the reaction of an alkyl halide with a sodium alkoxide or phenoxide.

items.stem: Which of the following shows the correct order of reactivity with Lucas reagent?
items.answer: 2-methylpropan-2-ol > butan-2-ol > butan-1-ol
items.markingKey: (c) 2-methylpropan-2-ol > butan-2-ol > butan-1-ol. Stability of the carbocation: 3° > 2° > 1°.

items.stem: Which structure corresponds to benzene-1,3-diol?
items.answer: m-C₆H₄(OH)₂
items.markingKey: (d) benzene-1,3-diol = m-C₆H₄(OH)₂.

items.stem: At a sugar mill near Kolhapur, Riya ferments 0.9 kg of glucose with yeast (zymase): C₆H₁₂O₆ → 2C₂H₅OH + 2CO₂. If the yield is 80%, calculate the mass of ethanol formed and the volume of CO₂ at STP (22.7 L mol⁻¹).
items.answer: 0.368 kg ethanol; 182 L CO₂

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “Hydration of propene in acid gives propan-1-ol.”
items.answer: It follows Markovnikov's rule and gives propan-2-ol.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: It follows Markovnikov's rule and gives propan-2-ol.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): The C–O–C bond angle in ethers is a little more than tetrahedral.
Reason (R): Ethers are more soluble in water than alcohols of similar mass.
